description:
print to a BAREWORD filehandle whose first argument is a GLOB is a whole-statement DROP: `print FOO * 2, "\n";` (FOO unknown, never opened) -- perl reads FOO as the filehandle and `*2` as the glob *main::2 (prints to the unopened handle: nothing, and the program continues); PCL announces `statement dropped ... Bug. Fell through. Missing case: []` and the statement dies at run time, so a following `print "end\n"` never runs.  PRE-EXISTING (base 5adcc156 identical).  Found by s513b (#2871): the static-parse review probe p16-constlater (`print PI * 2, "\n"; use constant PI => 3;`) printed 6 on main because the constant applied above its `use`; with #2871 the name is unknown there, as in perl, and the statement reaches this gap.  Repro:

  print FOO * 2, "\n"; print "end\n";        perl: end     PCL: (drop, dies)

Realistic shape: rare (an unknown ALL-CAPS word before `*`).  Fix site: the print filehandle-slot decision in PExpr (an unknown bareword followed by a term-starting `*`); probe the multiplication spelling `print FOO * 2` with a DECLARED sub FOO (must stay multiplication).

=== DONE (s514f, Opus) ===
PExpr's print path: after a bareword HANDLE is extracted, an Operator `*` followed by a digit Number or a Word is spliced into the one glob Symbol `*NAME` (the spelling PPI gives `*FOO` with no space, which already lowered).  So `print STDOUT *2`, `print FH * 2` (opened), `print STDOUT * Foo::bar` print the glob, and the task's unknown `print FOO * 2, "\n"; print "end\n"` prints `end` (= perl: the never-opened handle).  A constant / `()` sub is not a handle (the existing is_fh decision), so `print K * 2` still multiplies.  SKIPPED for a word this file declares as a sub: perl CALLS it there (`sub FOO {3} print FOO * 2` is FOO(*2,"\n") -> 3) -- that stays a LOUD drop; the general declared-sub-in-handle-slot silent wrong is #3182 (filed).  `print STDOUT (LIST)` dying "Undefined subroutine &main::STDOUT" filed as #3183.  Guard Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t +1 (fails on base).  The task's premise "a DECLARED sub FOO must stay multiplication" is wrong for an UNPROTOTYPED sub (probed: perl calls it); it holds for `sub FOO () {3}` (probed: 6).
subject: `print FOO * 2, ...` (unknown bareword, then a glob) is a whole-statement DROP -- perl prints the glob to filehandle FOO
